clue.text: Worst ring women give

parts.note: to worst someone is to defeat them, which is to best them
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A jilted lover tells the women to hand back the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worst' looks like an adjective but is the verb meaning to defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestow is to present or confer something on another, a formal synonym for handing it over.

clue.text: One who's left with a will?

definitions.text: One who's left with a will?

parts.words: One who's left with a will?
parts.note: with a will suggests eagerness, but it means someone named in a testament to carry it out

explanation.definitionFit: An executor is the person appointed in a will to administer the estate.

clue.text: Part of church with intricate patterns

indicators.note: intricate means tangled or complicated, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A section of a church decorated with elaborate designs.
explanation.definitionFit: The transept is the cross-arm of a cruciform church, crossing the nave.

clue.text: Planning a rest in extensive riverbank

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the word for extensive

parts.note: extensive means wide

indicators.note: planning means arranging, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone plans a break on a broad stretch of riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Planning' rearranges A REST into ATERS, which goes inside WIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: The waterside is the land along the edge of a river or lake.

clue.text: Came across a number, say — a figure of speech

parts.note: to come across someone is to have met them

indicators.note: say signals that a word is pronounced rather than spelt, here the number spoken

parts.note: four is a number

explanation.surface: Someone encountered a figure and remarks on a turn of phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: The spoken number is respelt PHOR to finish the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A metaphor is a standard example of a figure of speech, describing one thing in terms of another.

clue.text: Motorway signs finishing — fear poor understanding

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI

indicators.note: finishing points to the last letter of the word

parts.note: apprehension is anxious fear

explanation.surface: Seeing motorway signs end, a driver is anxious and confused.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a motorway out of London; the digit 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A misapprehension is a mistaken belief, a failure to understand correctly.

clue.text: The world of learning made difficult in a church

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the other pieces

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: difficult suggests the letters are awkwardly rearranged

explanation.surface: Academic life is made hard within a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficult' turns MADE into ADEM, which goes inside A plus CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Academe is the academic community, the world of universities and scholarship.

clue.text: Success — the girl's almost top up to now

parts.note: a hit is a success
her is the possessive for a girl

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

explanation.surface: A girl's hit nearly tops the charts so far.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitherto means until this point in time, so far.

clue.text: Make do with raised kerb

indicators.note: make means construct, so the letters are made into a new word

explanation.surface: Someone improvises using a raised kerb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make do' looks like a phrase for improvising; 'Make' is the anagram signal and 'with' joins the two fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: The roadside is the edge of a road, where the kerb runs.

clue.text: Target set when following races at sea

indicators.note: following places the word for when after the rearranged letters
set here means arranged into a new order, so the letters of target are rearranged

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as the sun rose'

explanation.surface: An aim is fixed for the time after some sailing contests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' rearranges TARGET into REGAT; AS then follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Regattas are sporting events made up of boat races, typically on sea or river.

clue.text: Major part of seductive woman's refrain

indicators.note: major part means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a mantrap is slang for an alluring, seductive woman

explanation.surface: Most of a temptress's song is a repeated chorus.
explanation.walkthrough: MANTRAP loses its last letter P.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a phrase repeated over and over, like the recurring line of a song.

clue.text: Away kit is better

parts.note: someone away is out
a sports team's kit is its strip

explanation.surface: A football fan claims the team's away kit is superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is the verb here, and 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstrip a rival is to surpass or exceed them, which is to better them.

clue.text: Still on board for this game?

indicators.note: on board means aboard a ship, so the word for still sits within the steamship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the vessel one boards
still can mean level, flat or even

explanation.surface: A question asks whether a board game is still being played.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'on board' is being inside a ship, SS. Sevens is seven-a-side rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: Sevens is the seven-a-side version of rugby union, a game in its own right.

clue.text: Strait-laced girl's flower?

parts.note: strait-laced means prudish or prim
Rose is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A prim young woman has a favourite bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The primrose is a pale yellow spring wildflower of the genus Primula.

clue.text: Shocked by teacher valued in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing signals that the words are judged by how they sound

parts.note: Sir is how British schoolchildren address a male teacher; prized means valued

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked by a teacher they admired, as heard.
explanation.walkthrough: SIR PRIZED is said just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be surprised is to be startled or taken aback, a milder form of shocked.

clue.text: Bother doctor with a temperature

explanation.surface: Someone pesters the physician about a fever.
explanation.definitionFit: Drat is a mild exclamation of annoyance, used just like the interjection bother.

clue.text: Follower's punishment not popular

indicators.note: not means without, so the popular word is removed

parts.note: discipline can mean punishment
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A follower is punished for being unpopular.
explanation.definitionFit: A disciple is a devoted follower of a teacher or leader.

clue.text: Precise bill put in front of minister

indicators.note: put in front of places the bill before the minister

parts.note: AC is an abbreviation for account, a bill
a curate is an assistant minister in a parish

explanation.surface: A bill is presented to a clergyman, with exact figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means correct in every detail, exact.

clue.text: Where sweat appears from soldiers during exercises?

indicators.note: during means within, so the soldiers sit inside the exercises

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A question about troops getting sweaty during drill.
explanation.definitionFit: Pores are the tiny openings in the skin through which perspiration emerges.

clue.text: Disheartened people stood for election with miners each year

indicators.note: disheartened means losing the heart, the middle letters, leaving only the outside

parts.note: to stand for election is to run
NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers in Britain

explanation.surface: Gloomy people stand for office alongside miners annually.
explanation.definitionFit: Per annum is Latin for yearly, used for annual rates.

clue.text: Way boxing permit is a risky game

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the way surrounds the permit

parts.note: a route is a way
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A permit for boxing is a gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino gambling game played with a spinning wheel.

clue.text: Pass on cost of assault by engineers

indicators.note: by means beside, so the engineers stand next to the assault

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a charge is a headlong attack

explanation.surface: Engineers launch an attack and bill someone for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To recharge a cost is to bill it on to someone else, passing the expense along.

clue.text: Relate possible action when votes are checked

definitions.meaning: to tell or narrate a story

definitions.text: possible action when votes are checked
definitions.meaning: a second tally of ballots in a close result

explanation.definitionFit: To recount is to narrate, and a recount is a second count of votes.

clue.text: Depressing feature of car for chicks?

definitions.meaning: the pedal pushed down to change gear
a group of young birds hatched together

explanation.definitionFit: A car's clutch pedal is pressed down, and a brood of hatchlings is called a clutch.

clue.text: No marines join forces, by and large

parts.note: taken as written
RM stands for Royal Marines
to ally is to join forces with someone

explanation.surface: Forces unite without the marines, more or less.
explanation.definitionFit: Normally means usually or as a rule, the same sense as the idiom by and large.

clue.text: Disease spread by case of pleural fever

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so only its first and last letters are used

parts.note: ague is an old word for a malarial fever

explanation.surface: An illness passed on through a type of lung fever.
explanation.definitionFit: Plague is a deadly infectious disease, historically the bubonic plague.

clue.text: Unhealthy, dismissing origins of all raging madness

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so these letters are removed from the longer word

parts.note: insanitary means dirty and unhealthy

indicators.note: the origins of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Something unhygienic, losing all rage, is plain lunacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origins of' gives A and R, taken out of INSANITARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Insanity is a state of mental derangement, a synonym for madness.

clue.text: Where seats are available for those standing

definitions.text: Where seats are available for those standing

parts.words: Where seats are available for those standing
parts.note: seats sounds like chairs in a hall, but these are parliamentary seats and those standing are candidates

explanation.definitionFit: Candidates stand for office at a vote, and parliamentary seats are won or lost there.

clue.text: Stifle study covering a politician

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so the study surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a den is a private study
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician hidden in a study suppresses something.
explanation.definitionFit: To dampen enthusiasm is to stifle or deaden it.
